prompt: Use case: stylized-concept, art-direction paintover of an existing game location. Image 1 is a current in-game screenshot of the Mega Park, a large concrete skate park set into rugged volcanic rock in a forested valley of the island in the game Yorimichi, seen from the western hills with the volcano on the left. Image 2 is another place in the same game and shows the art direction: soft painterly low-poly shapes, flat matte shading, pale lavender-grey rocks, autumn maples and ginkgos in rust, orange and gold, dark green pines, soft green grass, a clean blue sky. Repaint image 1 from exactly the same camera and composition as the improved AFTER version: the paintover a lead environment artist makes to show the team, concretely, what to change. Every skating structure stays exactly as it is, in the same place with the same shape: the concrete decks, ramps, bowls, walls, stairs, the white buildings and the wooden sign on the rock. Improve the surroundings and the rocks with specific, buildable changes. The forest round the park becomes denser and more beautiful: trees grouped in natural clumps of one species with a few small clearings, a varied canopy of different heights, a darker green understory of bushes, ferns and bamboo grass between the trunks, fallen leaves in drifts, and a soft forest edge of shrubs where the trees meet the rock and the concrete. The ground is no longer one flat green: leaf litter, darker moss under the trees, worn earth paths and grass tufts. The rocks become more beautiful: coherent weathered volcanic rock with clear horizontal layers and vertical joints, lighter sunlit tops and cooler shaded faces, moss and grass only on the top ledges, small maples, pines and shrubs rooted in the cracks, scree and boulders at their feet blending into the forest floor. The lone lollipop-shaped trees standing on the rock tops against the sky become clusters of shorter, wind-shaped pines and maples that crown the rim. Keep the volcano view. Keep the park rugged, with a raw skate-spot character. Stay in the game's style with its low-poly leaf-card trees; do not turn it photoreal. No people, no UI, no labels, no text.
